question: Q4 alternatives to seven 36-bit lanes
number: Alternatives built and checked: eight 32-bit lanes with lane-isolated add ((a&H)+(b&H)) ^ ((a^b)&T), 6 ops per two-word add: 1,080 ops = 135 per step, worse by 0.667 bit; seven 34-bit lanes 622 = 88.86, worse by 0.064; one lane per word: 595 ops = 0.9326 unit per step (folding alone beats the organizer's 638 by 7 percent, packing gives the factor 7). Not built: a cheaper rotation (4 operations) was looked for in the guard-bit layout and is not possible for pitch 36 (the shifted neighbour bits land inside the kept range for r > 4); a multiplication-based rotate needs a multiply primitive the model does not list.
notes: universe cell blake3-r3|MACHINE.WIDTH|MACHINE|Q4. The rotation remark is an argument, not a run.
reopen_if: a 4-operation rotation of packed lanes (saves up to 80 ops per batch, 0.2 bit), or a multiply primitive in the cost model
